# pkginspectr

<!-- badges: start -->

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/ddauber/pkginspectr/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/ddauber/pkginspectr)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/ddauber/pkginspectr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ddauber/pkginspectr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`pkginspectr` lets you peek inside R packages. It inspects local folders as well as packages downloaded from GitHub or CRAN and returns tidy tibbles that are easy to work with.

Key functions include:

-   `pkg_structure()` – counts files, folders, R scripts, tests, docs and data.
-   `pkg_lines()` – counts lines of code, comments, roxygen and blank lines, in `R/` and in tests.
-   `pkg_summary()` – both of the above in one table.
-   `pkg_plot()` (or just `plot()`) – draws simple but customisable bar charts of the results in the console.

Counts are designed to be trustworthy: lines are classified with R's own parser, and only files that `R CMD build` would ship are counted (`.Rbuildignore`, `.git/` and friends are skipped), so a local folder and a CRAN release of the same package give comparable results.

## Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ddauber/pkginspectr")
```

## Inspect a package

Want a quick overview of what’s inside an R package? `pkg_structure()` counts files, R scripts, tests, documentation and data. Here we use the small example package that ships with `pkginspectr`:

```{r inspect-package}
library(pkginspectr)

pkg_structure(pkginspectr_example())
```

`path` can be a local folder, a GitHub repository (`"owner/repo"`, optionally `"owner/repo@v1.0.0"`) or a CRAN package (`"desc"`, or an older release such as `"cran::desc@1.4.0"`). Downloads are cached for the rest of the R session, or across sessions with `cache = "persistent"`.

## Compute code statistics

Go beyond file counts and see how much code is really there. `pkg_lines()` breaks the lines in `R/`, `tests/` and `data-raw/` down by type (code, comment, roxygen, blank) and by location; each breakdown adds up to `total_lines`.

```{r pkg-lines}
pkg_lines(pkginspectr_example())
```

Files listed in `.Rbuildignore` are skipped by default; use `include_ignored = TRUE` to count them too. Need both tables? `pkg_summary()` returns them together and downloads each package only once.

## Visualise in the console

No need for heavy graphics — `pkg_plot()`, or simply `plot()`, renders Unicode bar charts right in your terminal. Each metric is shown as a share of its total:

```{r plot-pkg}
pkg_lines(pkginspectr_example()) |>
  plot()
```

You can customise the look to meet your needs: bars are just glyphs and ANSI colours, so you can tweak:

-   colours (`text_col`, `bar_col`, `bg_col`),
-   bar shape (`glyph`, `start`, `end`),
-   scale/fit (`max_bars`), or
-   add a custom title (`title`).

## Compare multiple packages

Compare packages side by side — perfect for exploring codebases or teaching.

```{r inspect-multiple, message = FALSE}
pkg_structure(c(
  "ddauber/pkginspectr",
  "ddauber/tidycomp",
  "ddauber/r4np"
)) |>
  pkg_plot(type = "metric")
```

Here `type = "metric"` switches from a per‑package breakdown to a metric‑centric view: one panel per metric, with bars scaled to the largest package.

See `vignette("pkginspectr")` for a full tour.

This package is meant to be a small and fun package with some useful functionality. Enjoy exploring your own R packages (as much as others’ packages)!
